proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: Ingrid sent us the full cost sheet for our basement: framing, electrical, HVAC, drywall, flooring, her fee and a 10% contingency. We used about half of the contingency and she showed us exactly where it went. Final number came in 3% over the starting budget.
reviews.name: Erik J.

reviews.text: We wanted a guest bedroom in the basement and learned it needed an egress window to count. They cut the foundation, set the well with a drain and the room passed inspection the first time.
reviews.name: Hannah V.

reviews.text: Every allowance had a number next to it: tile, faucets, lighting. When we picked a more expensive tile, the change order showed the difference to the dollar before they ordered it.
reviews.name: Marcus O.

reviews.text: Our 1915 house on the east side had knob-and-tube wiring hidden in one wall. They found it during the walk-through, priced it before demo, and it was in the budget from day one instead of a surprise.
reviews.name: Clare P.

reviews.text: The addition footings went in late April and the roof was on by early October, before the snow. The weekly cost update showed what had been billed and what was left.
reviews.name: Tom B.

reviews.text: My mother moved in with us and needed a shower she could walk into. They widened two doorways, put blocking in the walls for grab bars and built a curbless shower. She uses it every day without help.
reviews.name: Anita R.

reviews.text: Kitchen quote was eleven pages, one line per trade. Nobody else gave us anything like it. We knew where every dollar was going before we signed.
reviews.name: Joel F.

proof.guarantee: Our open-book promise: our fee is fixed on the cost sheet, and every change is priced before work starts.
